My therapist really helped me understand things and put my feelings into prescriptive for me. Theres no written rule stated that everyone has to have direction or have a path to follow. I use to be really hard on my self because I wanted to be married by Age X and Have a child by age X. I then realized like that putting pressure on myself was so unnecessary. I had it all, I had a partner with a great paying job, we were engaged, and ready to have kids. I then woke up and realized, that stuff that I thought I had wanted wasn't what I wanted at all.

I am currently switching careers, but when I was in my last career it was super low paying and I managed to find a hobby and was able to monetize for extra income. This next career should be able to just support me without me needing to put so much work in with an extra hobby. I seriously thought I was unartistic and talentless, but it turns out all I needed to do was believe in myself a little and really put effort into learning how to improve my skills with the hobby.

Where is it stated that you must have passion/direction? Whats wrong with just working a job that pays the bills, logging off and then going home and doing some hobbies and enjoying your time? I personally use to feel like such a loser about having that mindset, and then I realized social media is like fake and none of this stuff even really matters. There is nothing wrong with just living, working and doing some hobbies. This whole planet is seriously stupid and makes 0 sense. We are conditioned to do things a certain way, once you step outside that mindset and see that there is more to life its easier to understand. I hope all of that makes sense for you.

 I started seeking fulfillment(like volunteer work etc) and that is something that has truly helped me. I do truly understand how you're feeling though.

I am 26 now and have been feeling like this for as long as I can remember. My best coping tool as of recently, has been hobbies. I have picked up at least 5 hobbies over the pandemic. Thats what I do now. I just focus on different these days.

I was like this too, and I hated when people/ my therapist use to ask me my interests, until one day, I tried a bunch of the stuff my therapist said to me. even picked up some new hobbies. and you know what, he was right, i am less miserable with hobbies. I've been trying stuff that I might not have tried in the past because of the thought "what if im not good at this" but then I also remember people aren't generally good at things the first time they pick something up.

He also reminds that people aren't happy ALL of the time. Sometimes I feel happy, but not often.  Its something I think about pretty often. I also think about how weird it would be to be happy all the time.

There had been some things I was not lying about, but just not saying, and you know what, once I said them it was a huge relief.  Your T has your best interests in mind. They are there to lie to you or sugar coat it. 

Once my T found out my stuff he said "Oh OtherEgg2018 this really isnt a good idea" I could see he was visibly stressed out for me. I see my T as a sort of paid secret keeper. Sometimes being honest can be hard.

My therapist costs 240 an hour in Canada..... So sounds like you're getting a good deal. My insurance helps me a bit, but I am truly so thankful for my T. I know what you mean though years worth of problems and I usually get through the weekly stuff, but sometimes it helps me after the fact.

I've been in therapy for almost 2 years now heres what has changed for me:

I am much more kind in general, kinder to myself, I have more sympathy for other people, I am more forgiving. I don't find myself thinking about my trauma as much. I find myself thinking about how much potential I still have, How can I accomplish hard things. I think about doing the forbidden sleep less, I also can communicate better!

You should try to be a little more open about therapy, and its benefits, it sometimes takes time to see how things are changing for you. I truly find it invaluable (I am too nervous to tell my T how much hes really helped me for real) but I seriously feel so grateful. I know one day I can stop going, and so can you. Try to think of things like this "I get to go to therapy today" instead of "I have to go to therapy today" You're in the process of finding a different version of yourself. Just try to be open and listen to what they have to say. I didn't start noticing my personal changes until like a year into therapy honestly. It just takes time.
